minimalism_descent: Closed the round-2 gap with one small pure helper (_new_side_order_ok, ~30 LOC of logic) plus a single guard call in _segment_is_faithful and two docstring bullets. No new data structure and no second language heuristic: the helper reuses the LCS survivor indices already computed as kept_merged and the seg_tokens already built by _build_segments. It classifies each declared new line as before/after/between the marker(s) from token positions and enforces the constraint on the concrete unmatched merged indices, so nothing is recomputed. The guard is inserted before the deletion shortcut (a wrong-side new line can violate with zero deletions) and gated on has_marker so replacement zones and no-marker segments are untouched. No threshold, public API, dependency, tldr, or tree-sitter change; the prior expected-output synthesizer was NOT reintroduced. Net +75 lines in chunked_merge.py, all additive.

corrections: No existing oracle was weakened, deleted, skipped, xfail'd, or rewritten. All 111 prior focused cases remain enabled and pass unchanged; only additive test functions and two module-level test helpers were appended.

Round-2 (0039c6d) discovery #2 in REP-W-003 explicitly documented that the invariant validator 'intentionally does not pin a marker-inserted new line's exact position relative to surviving originals.' DEC-001/ATT-004 supersedes that non-guarantee for the before-first-marker and after-last-marker positions, which the text_match contract fixes; the between-markers position remains intentionally unconstrained, so that documented boundary is preserved.
discoveries: Root cause confirmed exactly as the blocking finding: _segment_is_faithful verified new-vs-new order (new_in_merged == new_all) and survivor-vs-survivor order (LCS) independently, but never compared an unmatched new occurrence's merged index against the matched survivors' merged indices. All three blocking corrupt merges keep the survivor multiset intact and only relocate the new line, so they slipped through at 1.0.

deterministic_edit is the semantic reference and is self-consistent with the new guard: probing the 7 parity rows shows before-marker new lines are emitted before the preserved gap and after-marker new lines after it (e.g. new-before-marker -> 'z = 99' precedes 'b = 2','c = 3'; new-after-marker -> 'r = 3' follows 'q = 2'; marker-key-replacement -> 'self._data = OrderedDict()' precedes surviving 'self.count = 0'). Enforcing the side-order therefore tightens the validator toward deterministic_edit rather than diverging from it — the parity matrix stays green.

Using occurrence indices (kept_merged from LCS + the ordered unmatched merged indices) rather than line values is what makes repeated-identical survivors safe: the guard rejects an after-marker line placed between two identical dup() survivors because its merged index is less than the last survivor's, which a set/count-based check could not detect.
